Unlike broad-lined quasars, radio galaxies lack a dominant nuclear point source in the rest-frame optical--UV, enabling direct constraints on host-galaxy structure and its relation to the radio jet. We analyze Hubble Space Telescope (HST) WFC3/IR (rest-frame optical) and WFC3/UVIS (rest-frame UV) imaging of the $z>1$ 3CR radio galaxies. Beyond confirming the classical rest-frame UV alignment effect, we find that the radio jets preferentially align with the major axes of the smooth rest-frame optical hosts, extending the alignment to the older stellar component. The projected axes of candidate mergers in eight systems preferentially follow the radio axes. This multiscale coherence suggests a common projected axis linking the radio source to host assembly, perhaps established by repeated mergers or anisotropic infall. We test scattered quasar light and jet-triggered star formation as origins of the UV emission along this axis. The much shallower-than-expected radial decline in UV surface brightness disfavors simple scattering as the dominant population-wide origin, while ionized-gas masses further disfavor electron scattering. The required dust masses are small relative to global reservoirs, so dust scattering remains feasible in individual regions. Comparing stellar-population ages and jet-propagation times, we identify seven UV-emitting regions as strong candidates for recently initiated jet-triggered star formation. Together, these alignments reveal an assembly-linked direction along which jets may shock or compress material and hidden-quasar radiation may illuminate it.

entries.title: Solid-state formation of H$_2$CS and CH$_3$SH in molecular clouds: Carbon-initiated reactions with atomic and molecular hydrogen
entries.abstract: The solid-state formation pathways of thioformaldehyde (H$_2$CS) and methanethiol (CH$_3$SH) in dense molecular clouds remain poorly constrained. We investigate carbon-initiated reactions in hydrogen sulfide (H$_2$S) ice in the presence of atomic or molecular hydrogen. We co-deposited H$_2$S, ground-state atomic carbon, and H or H$_2$ at 10 K under ultra-high vacuum. We monitored the reaction products using reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy (RAIRS) and characterized their thermal desorption using temperature-programmed desorption (TPD) with quadrupole mass spectrometry. Gas-phase ab initio calculations were used to assess pathways to CH$_3$SH formation. Atomic carbon reacted with H$_2$S at 10 K to form H$_2$CS, detected as both monomers and H$_2$CS-derived oligomers. With atomic H, successive H addition to H$_2$CS leads to CH$_3$SH. With molecular H$_2$, CH$_3$SH also forms efficiently. The results support an alternative pathway in which C reacts with H$_2$ to form CH$_2$, which abstracts H from H$_2$S. The resulting CH$_3$ and SH radicals can then recombine to form CH$_3$SH. The infrared bands and TPD fragmentation patterns support the formation of H$_2$CS and CH$_3$SH in the ice at 10 K. These findings expand the set of viable solid-state pathways to sulfur-bearing molecules and constrain models of sulfur chemistry in prestellar environments.

entries.title: Cosmological structure formation in ultralight dark matter
entries.abstract: An important challenge in cosmology is to describe the formation of galaxies and structures, starting from small inhomogeneities in the early Universe, which later grew and formed the so- called dark matter halos. We consider the dark matter to be composed of ultralight bosons and simplify the general complex problem of halo formation by using the time-dependent variational analysis approach. This yields, for the first time, a fully analytical equation for the time-evolution of perturbations towards isolated haloes. We follow the evolution of the halo size and density during different stages of its formation, revealing the role of the background density, Universe expansion, and quantum pressure.

entries.title: Welopō'ai: A peculiar triple system 8 pc from the Sun
entries.abstract: Context. We report the serendipitous discovery of a white dwarf companion to the M4 V dwarf Welopo'ai Aa (IRAS 21500+5903) during a radial-velocity search for exoplanets with SPIRou. The system is located at 8.46 pc and forms a hierarchical triple with a more distant white dwarf, which has no known analogue within 30 pc. Aims. We characterise the orbital architecture and component masses through a joint Keplerian fit of radial velocities and astrometry, derive the physical parameters of the M dwarf and both white dwarfs, and discuss the implications for common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple dynamics. Methods. We obtained radial velocity measurements with SPIRou spread over 4.8 yr, revealing a large-amplitude signal ($\sim$16 km/s peak-to-peak) that is inconsistent with planetary companions. Follow-up speckle imaging with 'Alopeke at Gemini North and near-infrared (NIR) imaging with GNIRS confirmed a white dwarf companion at sub-arcsecond separation. Results. The system comprises an inner binary with a semi-major axis of $4.644 \pm 0.017$ au ($P \approx 9.83$ yr), consisting of the primary M4 V ($M = 0.4189^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072} M_\odot$) and a white dwarf companion ($M = 0.6180^{+0.0046}_{-0.0045} M_\odot$, $T_{\rm eff} \sim 5210 \pm 320$ K, cooling age 5.3-5.5 Gyr). This inner pair lies at a projected separation of 123.9 au ($P > 1000$ yr) from a previously known white dwarf. The dynamically determined mass of the inner white dwarf is one of only a handful of such measurements for white dwarfs within 20 pc, and the most precise, at the sub-percent (0.7%) level. Conclusions. This system is the closest known triple containing multiple white dwarfs and offers direct dynamical constraints on common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple stability. Furthermore, a tentative near-infrared (IR) excess towards the inner white dwarf further hints at circumstellar dust.

entries.title: Interpretable attention-based neural posterior estimation for fast radio burst cosmology
entries.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe the integrated free-electron density along extragalactic sightlines and can be used to study late-time cosmic evolution. Conventional Bayesian analyses require repeated evaluations of computationally expensive likelihoods, making inference increasingly challenging as FRB catalogs grow. In this work, we develop an interpretable attention-based neural posterior estimator (AttNPE) for rapid posterior inference of the physical parameters from FRB catalogs with measured redshifts. The attention encoder compresses the catalog into a low-dimensional representation, and a conditional masked autoregressive flow maps samples from a base distribution to the seven-dimensional posterior. AttNPE yields posterior distributions in close agreement with Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), recovering the parameter correlations in both simulated and observed FRB catalogs. For the observed catalog, AttNPE generates $5\times10^4$ posterior samples in $0.036$~s after training, compared with $72.8$~h for the reference MCMC run, giving an elapsed-time ratio of $O(10^6)$. The attention-weight analysis shows that intermediate-redshift FRBs ($0.3\leq z<0.7$) account for the largest share of the total attention averaged over simulated catalogs following the observed redshift distribution, consistent with the combined influence of source abundance and redshift-dependent sensitivity. These results demonstrate the potential of interpretable neural posterior estimation for efficient and repeated inference in FRB cosmology.

entries.title: Characterization of the $b$-anisotropy for axisymmetric early-type galaxies in TNG50
entries.abstract: High-quality observations reveal that internal dynamics of axisymmetric ETGs can be more complicated than commonly adopted in modelizations based on the Jeans equations (JEs), with the identity of the radial and vertical velocity dispersions. A well known generalization is obtained by solving the JEs with the prescription of a proportionality factor $b$ between the radial and vertical velocity dispersions; in its simplest form $b$ is assumed constant, while in recent studies $b=b(z)$. We investigate the properties of the $b$ parameter and of the other kinematical decomposition parameters commonly adopted in modeling in a sample of ETGs taken from the high-resolution cosmological simulations TNG50. From a selection of highly axisymmetric and passive TNG50 (satellite and central) galaxies at equilibrium, we recovered the maps of $b(R,z)$ and of other important kinematic quantities entering the JEs. In all the selected galaxies the only significantly non-zero velocity streaming component is the azimuthal one, and the velocity dispersion tensor is cylindrically aligned. The maps of $b$ are clearly not constant, and not stratified over planes, instead they present a common structure, with the largest values values near the center, and a wedge structure at large (cylindrical) radii. A phenomenological formula for $b(R,z)$ to be used in applications is proposed. Also the other decomposition parameters are non-constant. No significant differences are found as a function of galaxy flattening and mass, while some difference is observed between satellite and central galaxies. The internal dynamics of the TNG50 galaxies present interesting regularities, worth of investigation. On the other hand, in Jeans based studies of real galaxies some simple assumptions for the choice of anisotropy and kinematical decomposition parameters do not seem appropriate. [abridged]

entries.title: Computation of complex dust grain optical properties: Optimisation method by equivalent representation (OMER)
entries.abstract: Computing the optical properties of dust grains is important for understanding various astrophysical environments. However, the numerical methods used to compute these properties require significant computing resources for irregularly shaped or inhomogeneous particles that are representative of realistic grown dust. This study aims to provide an efficient yet accurate Discrete dipole approximation (DDA) computation method for large aggregates with 'complex' monomers and structural details or compositional inhomogeneities. We propose the optimisation method by equivalent representation (OMER) method, which uses optimisation of the optical properties of a known monomer to find an equivalent homogeneous sphere. This sphere can then be used as a substitute for the complex monomer in large aggregates. The method provides a good approximation of complex monomers, as demonstrated in test cases involving large aggregates. Compared to existing methods, OMER shows greater accuracy, particularly in the range from visible to submillimetre wavelengths. The gain in computing time depends on the grain but can exceed two orders of magnitude. The proposed method provides a fast and accurate approximation for estimating the optical properties of materials with complex shapes and paves the way for efficient computation cross-sections for complex dust grain aggregates with thin core-mantle structures or hierarchical aggregates of large sizes.

entries.title: Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with mass estimates verifiable in Gaia Data Release 4
entries.abstract: Gaia Science Alerts provide an all-sky stream of photometric transients, including events consistent with gravitational microlensing. For such events, forthcoming epoch astrometry from the Gaia mission offers the possibility of testing photometric lens mass predictions. While microlensing parallax inferred from the photometric light curve can constrain the event geometry, a direct lens mass measurement additionally requires the angular Einstein radius, which may be accessible through astrometric microlensing. We aim to construct a pre-Data-Release-4 (DR4) sample of Gaia microlensing events for which the available photometry provides a measurable microlensing-parallax signal. This allows us to derive statistical predictions for the lens mass and distance. We forward-modelled these events to predict the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal in Gaia DR4. We identify 56 Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with 71 point-source point-lens solutions with annual parallaxes that satisfy our fit-quality, posterior-boundedness, and parallax-significance criteria. Lens masses and distances were inferred using two prior-based frameworks, pyLIMASS and the Besançon Galaxy Model, which combine the measured microlensing parameters and Gaia source information with stellar-population and Galactic models. These inferred parameters were used to simulate Gaia DR4-like along-scan astrometry and estimate the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal. The inferred lens masses and distances remain strongly prior-dependent without a direct angular Einstein radius measurement. Among the 284 event-solution-prior branches, 47 are classified as high-confidence astrometric detections using Gaia DR4-like simulations. These predictions can be tested once epoch astrometry is released in Gaia DR4.

entries.title: JCMT POL-2 observations of NGC 253: evidence for large-scale reordering of magnetic fields in giant molecular cloud complexes
entries.abstract: In this paper we present observations of the magnetic field of the starburst galaxy NGC 253 made in polarized 850 $μ$m dust emission using the POL-2 polarimeter on the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT). While the magnetic field typically traces the galactic spiral structure, we see significant deviations in field direction associated with the presence of stellar and/or supernova feedback, with the mean plane-of-sky magnetic field direction offset 24$^{\circ}$ from the galactic plane. Polarization fraction is anticorrelated with total 850 $μ$m intensity, with a power-law index of 0.72$\pm$0.03. Using the Fasano-Franceschini test, we find that the positions of POL-2 detections and radio sources in the spiral arms are inconsistent with one another, indicative of depolarization resulting from magnetic fields being tangled on scales smaller than the 240 pc JCMT 850 $μ$m beam in sites of star formation and feedback. Moreover, in both the starburst superwind and in one star-forming clump in the spiral arms, we observe a magnetic field direction consistent with being directed out of the plane of the galaxy. We thus hypothesise that magnetic fields in the giant molecular clouds (GMCs) of NGC 253 are undergoing an evolutionary sequence from a relatively ordered field parallel to the spiral arms in the pre-star-formation gas, to a complex field caused by the interplay of turbulence, gravity and small-scale feedback in relatively young GMCs, to a field that is reordered out of the plane of the galaxy as large-scale HII region expansion reshapes the gas and dust of galactic spiral arms.

entries.title: A $10^5\,M_\odot$ Black Hole in the Bulgeless Spiral Galaxy IC 342: First Stellar-Dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ Measurement with Keck/OSIRIS LGS-AO
entries.abstract: We present the first direct stellar-dynamical measurement of an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) in IC 342, a nearby nearly face-on ($i\approx31^\circ$) bulgeless spiral at $D=3.45\pm0.13$ Mpc, using near-infrared integral-field spectroscopy with Keck/OSIRIS LGS-AO. The heavy foreground extinction ($A_{\mathrm{F814W}}\approx0.74$ mag) renders the nucleus inaccessible to optical spectroscopy, making $K$-band observations at $\sim$2.3 $μ$m the only viable path to high-resolution nuclear kinematics. Two-dimensional stellar kinematics extracted from the CO bandheads via pPXF at $0.062''$ resolution reveal a central velocity dispersion rising from $\sim$42 km s$^{-1}$ at $r\gtrsim0.2''$ to a peak of $\sim$49 km s$^{-1}$, providing kinematic evidence for a central dark mass within the nuclear star cluster (NSC; $M_\mathrm{NSC}\approx1.17\times10^7~M_\odot$). Modeling these kinematics with an ensemble of four JAM models, spanning cylindrical and spherical velocity-ellipsoid alignments and two PSF representations, combined with an MGE mass model constructed from a three-Sérsic plus exponential-disk decomposition of archival HST/WFC3 F814W imaging and incorporating a physically motivated stellar mass-to-light ratio gradient, driven by the young central NSC population, yields $M_\mathrm{BH}=(1.95\pm0.61)\times10^5~M_\odot$. Accounting for this stellar population gradient is essential for the detection: standard constant-$M/L$ models systematically overestimate the central stellar mass, hiding the BH signature and yielding only an upper limit. The stellar orbits are near-isotropic ($β\approx0$), typical of fast-rotating late-type spirals. This measurement places IC 342 among the rare bulgeless spirals with a direct dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ at the IMBH mass scale, where both the NSC and BH are directly characterized, providing a new anchor for compact massive object co-evolution models.

entries.title: The infrared arc around $α$ Crucis: a weak interaction with a structured interstellar medium
entries.abstract: Infrared arc-shaped structures around early-type stars are commonly interpreted as stellar wind bow shocks, although their morphology may also be shaped by gas motions and density variations in the surrounding interstellar medium. We present a multiwavelength study of the infrared arc associated with the nearby $α$ Crucis system, comprising HD 108248 (B0.5 IV), HD 108249 (B1 V), and HD 108250 (B4 V). We combine WISE, Herschel, Planck, stellar astrometry, and eROSITA X-ray data to investigate the structure and its relation to the stellar components. The WISE W4 ridge extends over $\sim$0.65 pc and has a median PSF-corrected width of $\sim$0.037 pc. The HD 108248/HD 108249 pair lies $\sim$0.13 pc from the ridge, compared with $\sim$0.17 pc for HD 108250. Relative to the mean motion of the Lower Centaurus-Crux (LCC) subgroup of the Scorpius-Centaurus association, the close pair is consistent with LCC, whereas HD 108250 has a transverse peculiar velocity of only $\sim$1.8 km s$^{-1}$. Its motion lies within $\sim$23$^\circ$ of the geometrical symmetry axis of the infrared arc, but points in the opposite sense from the arc. Herschel maps show slightly higher median dust temperature ($ΔT_d\sim$0.8 K) and molecular-hydrogen column density ($ΔN_{\rm H2}\sim$7$\times$10$^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$) toward the W4-defined region than in the nearby background. On larger scales, Planck maps reveal a strongly structured microwave environment around the system. Both the HD 108248/HD 108249 pair and HD 108250 are detected by eROSITA, with the former approximately 60 times more luminous in X-rays. The combined morphology, kinematics, and dust properties do not support an unambiguous classical high-velocity bow-shock interpretation. Instead, the arc likely traces a weak interaction between the multiple stellar system and an inhomogeneous ambient medium.

entries.title: Early spectra of AT2017gfo from scaled 3D merger ejecta: mass--velocity distribution, 3D structure, and treatment of line opacity
entries.abstract: We present ARTIS radiative transfer calculations for neutron star merger ejecta with line-by-line opacities, wavelength-calibrated lanthanide data, and time-dependent r-process compositions and thermalisation, testing how the early kilonova depends on the mass-velocity distribution, dimensionality, and line treatment. We rescale 3D dynamical ejecta from a merger simulation in density and velocity to approximate AT2017gfo. Mass scaling alone provides good agreement with the bolometric light curve but inconsistent spectra. With velocities additionally halved, the model also reproduces the observed spectra at 1.4, 2.4, and (albeit less accurately) 3.4 days. The Sr II triplet contributes most to the 10500 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ peak, and La III and Gd III to the 13500 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ shoulder. Although hydrodynamically not fully self-consistent, this model is to our knowledge the first kilonova model based on calibrated atomic data that reproduces the light curve and main spectral features of the early AT2017gfo, suggesting that total (dynamical plus post-merger) ejecta with higher mass, lower velocity, and similar composition compared to our dynamical ejecta could explain AT2017gfo. A 2D azimuthal average mixes lanthanide-poor with lanthanide-rich regions, smooths the density, and makes the averaged model three times fainter at 1 day and redder throughout than the 3D model, highlighting the importance of 3D modelling. We compare the line-by-line macroatom treatment with expansion-opacity and line-binned schemes with thermal redistribution, using identical atomic data. Luminosities agree to $\lesssim 10$ per cent after 1 day, but the expansion-opacity scheme, unlike converged line-binned schemes, overestimates the spectral flux by up to 20 per cent, which can bias inferred abundances.

entries.title: The Gas-Phase Metallicity and Nitrogen abundances in typical galaxies at $z\sim5$
entries.abstract: The relation between stellar mass and gas-phase metallicity (MZR) is a key tracer of the baryon cycle in galaxies. JWST now gives access to rest-optical emission lines at z > 3, enabling unprecedented constraints on the chemical enrichment and the conditions of the interstellar medium of galaxies in the early Universe. In this work, we present the MZR at $z=3.8-6.6$ from stacked NIRCam/grism spectra of 1748 H$α$-selected star-forming galaxies compiled over an area of 320 arcmin$^2$. The simple H$α$ flux-limited selection allows us to measure representative [NII]$λ$6584/H$α$ and [SII]$λλ$6716,6731/ H$α$ ratios in stacks spanning $\rm log(M_\star/M_\odot)=8-10.2$, extending the upper mass range of previous high-redshift MZR measurements by $\sim1$ dex. Gas-phase metallicities are derived from these ratios using strong-line calibrations recently derived from high-redshift galaxies. The[NII]-based MZR has a slope $γ= 0.42^{+0.10}_{-0.07}$ and $12+\rm log(O/H) = 7.94^{+0.06}_{-0.09}$ at $\rm log(M_\star/M_\odot) = 9$, in broad agreement with recent empirical studies and hydrodynamical simulations. The [SII]-based relation yields a consistent slope and a $\sim0.3$ dex higher normalization, within the systematic uncertainties of strong-line calibrations. From the resolved [SII] doublet we infer a median electron density of $n_e = 184^{+226}_{-169}\,\rm cm^{-3}$. Combining [NII] and [SII], we indirectly estimate the N/O ratio and find that it follows the trend expected from primary and secondary nitrogen production, with no evidence for nitrogen enhancement in the HII region emission that dominates our galaxies. Our results provide a benchmark for the chemical enrichment and ISM conditions of typical star-forming galaxies at $z\sim5$ across a wide mass range.

entries.title: Investigating the Impact of SAX J1808.4-3658's Very Bright Thermonuclear X-ray Burst on the Accretion Disc with NICER
entries.abstract: We analyse a bright thermonuclear X-ray burst from the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar (AMXP) SAX J1808.4-3658, the brightest burst detected by \textit{NICER} to date, to explore interactions between thermonuclear burst radiation and the accretion disc. This burst features a remarkable soft (<1.5 keV) excess in its spectra. For the first time, we simultaneously detect a reflection signal and the signature of an evolving persistent component, with our fits producing a peak persistent scaling factor $f_{a,1} = 59.6\pm0.6$. We find a high peak reflection fraction ($f_{r,1} = 0.82\pm0.15$) and a peak bolometric burst blackbody flux below Eddington (0.68$L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$) despite signatures of photospheric radius expansion. We detect a raised $N_\mathrm{H}$ ($\approx$34% above persistent emission) and raised disc blackbody temperature ($\approx$15% above persistent emission) during the burst's tail. This is the first time that spectroscopic evidence consistent with burst-induced disc heating has been found. We interpret that disc heating could cause the disc to puff up and inhibit burst photons, explaining the high reflection fraction and below-Eddington burst luminosity during the burst peak. We find an increasing count rate starting from $\approx$150s before the burst onset. Spectral analysis revealed a thermal component that evolves towards hotter temperatures closer to the onset of the burst. This is the second detection of this phenomenon from an AMXP. Lastly, we find that both the double-peaked structure and the "pause" in the rise are energy-dependent.

entries.title: Rapid Equation of State Inference from Multiprobe Datasets
entries.abstract: Fully constraining the neutron star equation of state (EoS) requires combining observations from various channels that probe different density regimes. We perform a joint multimessenger inference of the equation of state using gravitational-wave observations from binary neutron star mergers, NICER mass-radius measurements of X-ray pulsars, and radio timing measurements of massive pulsars. We constrain the parametrized equation of state and perform Bayesian model selection among a set of candidate equations of state. The joint analysis produces a radius of $R_{1.4} = 11.93^{+1.02}_{-0.83} \, \rm km$ for a canonical $1.4 \, M_\odot$ neutron star, and a maximum non-rotating neutron star mass of $M_{\rm max} = 2.31^{+0.23}_{-0.23} \, M_\odot$ with $90\%$ credible intervals. Gravitational-wave and NICER observations constrain the equation of state at low to intermediate densities, while massive pulsar observations constrain it at high densities by requiring the equation of state to support the neutron star masses. We find no simple correlation between the stiffness of an EoS and Bayesian evidence because the observations probe the pressure at different density regimes. By combining constraints on the equation of state with Bayesian model selection using multimessenger data, our analysis connects macroscopic neutron star measurements to microscopic properties of candidate nuclear matter models.

entries.title: Discovery of HEC14: an ultra-faint stellar system in M31's outer halo at the globular cluster-dwarf galaxy boundary
entries.abstract: We present the discovery of HEC14, an ultra-faint stellar system near M31, visually identified in the Pan-Andromeda Archaeological Survey and characterised with deeper OSIRIS+@GTC imaging. HEC14's colour-magnitude diagram shows a clear red giant branch and a well-populated blue horizontal branch, indicating old (>10 Gyr), metal poor stellar populations. We find 912$^{+88}_{-80}$ kpc to be the best-fitting heliocentric distance to the satellite, consistent with M31's outer halo. With $M_{V} \sim -5.00^{+0.51}_{-0.44}$ and a half-light radius of $r_{\rm h} \sim 31^{+13}_{-9}$pc HEC14 lies in the size-luminosity gap between globular clusters and dwarf galaxies. The satellite therefore sits in the extended clusters (EC) regime, making it one of the faintest ECs discovered yet in M31. HEC14 is a new member of M31's halo EC population, whose origins remain unclear two decades after their discovery. We serendipitously find that HEC14's size and luminosity match theoretical predictions for dwarf galaxies with globular cluster-like sizes. Star formation history and/or spectroscopic studies are required to determine whether HEC14 (and possibly all ECs) is genuinely an extended globular cluster or a compact dwarf galaxy.

entries.title: Deep Multiwavelength Constraints on the Host Galaxies and Black-Hole Growth of Dwarf AGNs
entries.abstract: We present a multiwavelength population study of 56 X-ray-detected dwarf galaxies ($M_* < 3 \times 10^9 M_\odot$), comprising 31 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) and 25 galaxies (not satisfying AGN classification) in the Chandra Deep Fields North and South. Utilizing ultra-deep Chandra observations together with high-resolution JWST and HST imaging, we investigate the demographics, host-galaxy properties, environments, and cosmic evolution of accreting black holes in low-mass galaxies out to $z\approx4$. We find no statistically significant differences in either the local environments or non-parametric morphologies of X-ray AGNs relative to mass- and redshift-matched inactive dwarf galaxies. These results suggest that AGN activity in dwarf galaxies does not generally require ongoing major mergers or strong large-scale disturbances. Using a single power-law model for the specific accretion-rate distribution, we infer a positive cosmic evolution of dwarf-galaxy black-hole growth. Both the observed AGN fraction and the long-term average black-hole accretion rate increase toward higher redshift and show a positive stellar-mass dependence. Many dwarf AGNs exhibit weak optical and near-infrared AGN signatures, consistent with moderate accretion rates and, at high redshift, potentially enhanced obscuration. The small number of detected systems at $z>2$ limits definitive conclusions, but their hard X-ray colors suggest that obscuration may play an increasingly important role in the dwarf AGN population in the early universe. Our results support a picture in which black-hole growth in dwarf galaxies proceeds through largely stochastic or secular processes while gradually increasing in prevalence toward cosmic noon, providing new empirical constraints on the low-mass end of black hole-galaxy coevolution.

entries.title: Surrogate Modeling and Reduced-Order Methods in Gravitational-Wave Physics and Numerical Relativity: From Spectral Representations to Adaptive Compression
entries.abstract: The rapid expansion of gravitational-wave astronomy and high-precision numerical relativity has created an acute computational bottleneck: direct numerical integration of the Einstein field equations and high-dimensional Bayesian parameter estimation require millions of waveform evaluations that cannot be sustained by traditional solvers alone. Reduced-order modeling (ROM) and surrogate techniques have emerged as foundational tools to bridge this gap, compressing high-fidelity solution manifolds into compact, rapidly evaluable representations without sacrificing physical accuracy. This perspective reviews the mathematical pillars of projection-based reduced-order modeling---including Proper Orthogonal Decomposition, greedy basis selection, and the Empirical Interpolation Method---and traces their operational impact in gravitational-wave data analysis through surrogate waveform families and Reduced-Order Quadratures. We then examine the fundamental approximation barriers posed by slow Kolmogorov n-width decay in non-stationary, transient, and strongly nonlinear regimes, showing how adaptive hp-greedy domain partitioning and multi-scale spectral compression overcome these limits. Finally, we discuss how combining certified reduced-order structures with modern scientific machine learning and sensitivity-aware quantization provides a rigorous blueprint for next-generation detectors such as LISA, Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer.

entries.title: Infrared spectrum of the Type Iax supernova remnant Pa30
entries.abstract: The central star of Pa30 and its nebulosity offer one of the best opportunities to study a SN Iax explosion and its remnant. Pa30 is thought to be the product of the historical supernova explosion of 1181. No infrared spectroscopy of its extremely hot central star has hitherto been reported. Here, we present a 0.75-5 $μ$m spectrum taken by the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx), together with ground-based infrared spectra, at higher resolution, covering the 0.8-2.5 $μ$m region. The spectra contain very broad lines, which we have attempted to identify and model using the codes CMFGEN and CLOUDY. The CMFGEN modelling suggests that most of the lines are due to OVI. However, CLOUDY modelling, using expected theoretical abundances for the bound remnants of SN Iax explosions, provides evidence for the presence of coronal lines of Si, S, Mg, and Al arising from a shocked gas. This strengthens the suggestion that Pa30 is indeed the remnant of a SN Iax explosion.

entries.title: The GECKOS Survey: deriving bar properties in edge-on galaxies from molecular gas kinematics
entries.abstract: The characterisation of disc-connected structures such as bars and nuclear rings is a difficult task in edge-on galaxies. We present a simple method to derive bar position angles and lengths in edge-on galaxies using molecular gas kinematics from ALMA observations. Our approach exploits the geometry of bar-driven gas flows: assuming that cold molecular gas settles into an elliptical nuclear ring oriented orthogonally to the bar, the line-of-sight velocity of the nuclear ring varies predictably with bar viewing angle. Using only the observed nuclear ring velocity and a circular velocity derived from Multi-Gaussian Expansion (MGE) stellar mass models, we construct a grid of bisymmetric bar flow models spanning a range of radial and transverse velocities to constrain the bar position angle. We validate this methodology on a toy model and an isolated galaxy hydrodynamical simulation snapshot, demonstrating that the technique reliably distinguishes three viewing angle brackets: side-on (0° - 35°), intermediate (35° - 65°), and end-on (65° - 90°). Applying this method to six GECKOS Survey galaxies hosting boxy-peanut bulges with ALMA CO observations, we find four bars oriented side-on, one at an intermediate angle, and one end-on case (IC 1711), the latter confirming predictions from stellar kinematics alone. Derived nuclear ring sizes and deprojected bar lengths are broadly consistent with measurements from more face-on literature samples. This method offers a practical and computationally inexpensive means of constraining bar properties in edge-on galaxies, complementing full dynamical modelling approaches.

entries.title: Asteroseismology of AI Velorum: a prototype of high-amplitude delta Scuti stars
entries.abstract: AI Velorum is exceptional among high-amplitude δScuti (HADS) stars because of its multimode pulsations. Despite being an excellent target for asteroseismology, this prototype star has not been studied in detail. We determine the stellar parameters, age, and evolutionary stage of AI Vel, constrain envelope convection and convective core overshooting, and test three opacity data sets: OPAL, OP, and OPLIB. We analysed TESS photometry, ground-based Strömgren photometry, and HARPS spectroscopy. Modes were identified using photometric and spectroscopic methods, and empirical values of the non-adiabatic f-parameter were derived for both radial modes. Seismic modelling was performed within a Bayesian framework supported by Monte Carlo simulations. We confirm the radial nature of the two dominant modes and identify one non-radial mode as most likely an axisymmetric dipole or quadrupole mode. Within the explored parameter space, only OPAL models reproduce the observed position of AI Vel in the HR diagram, whereas OP and OPLIB models are too cool and underluminous. All seismic models favour inefficient envelope convection (mixing-length parameter alpha_{mlt}\lesssim 0.5). Including the non-radial mode substantially reduces the formal posterior uncertainties, but the ambiguity in its identification introduces additional model-dependent uncertainties. AI Vel is an evolved, slowly rotating star in the hydrogen shell-burning phase. Our results demonstrate the diagnostic power of combining pulsation frequencies with empirical f-parameters. The preference for OPAL opacities is consistent with results for several other HADS and SX Phoenicis stars but does not imply a general superiority of OPAL opacities.

entries.title: Cross-Dataset Inference of Central-Satellite Classification and Host Halo Masses from Galaxy neighbours with Machine Learning
entries.abstract: The classification of galaxies as centrals or satellites gives insight into the galaxy-halo connection. This, together with halo mass estimates, can be used to connect observed galaxy populations to underlying dark matter structure. To (1) classify galaxies as centrals or satellites and (2) estimate the host halo mass for centrals, we train XGBoost models on IllustrisTNG (TNG100) galaxies, using the distances (3D or projected (2+1)D redshift space) and $M_*$ of their ten nearest neighbours. We then test the model on EAGLE to measure its robustness after applying a simple domain-alignment step that corrects for a relative shift in the $M_*$ distribution between TNG100 and EAGLE. We further augment the training data by combining feature sets from neighbour samples with varying lower $M_*$ thresholds. On the TNG100 test set, the central/satellite classifier reaches purity and completeness $=0.97$ (0.95) in 3D (projected redshift) space at the threshold where purity=completeness, and the halo-mass regressor achieves $r^2$=0.98 (0.93) when evaluated on true centrals and $r^2=0.93$ (0.93) when evaluated on inferred centrals. Applied to EAGLE after alignment, the classifier achieves purity/completeness $=0.95$ (0.95), while halo-mass inference yields $r^2=0.91$ ($0.87$) for true centrals and $r^2=0.83$ (0.77) for inferred centrals; training-data augmentation most improves the halo-mass estimation task. Satellites misclassified as centrals underpredict the true masses of host halos, especially if they are closer to a lower mass halo's central than its own host's central and/or has a significantly lower $M_*$ than its own central. These results show that survey-accessible information such as projected separations and stellar masses - combined with simulation-trained models and domain alignment - can enable reliable central identification and host halo mass estimation to an $r^2\geq 0.85$.

entries.title: Deconstructing the cosmic baryon distribution with fast radio bursts
entries.abstract: The precise distribution of baryons in the Universe remains an open question in cosmology, as their highly diffuse nature hinders direct observation. However, mapping it is integral for precision cosmology in studies of gravitational lensing, galaxy evolution and the cosmic microwave background with current and upcoming surveys. We use fast radio bursts (FRBs) and their dispersion measures (DMs) to probe and localise this baryon distribution in the large-scale structure (LSS). Using IllustrisTNG simulations, we classify the LSS into eight bins of increasing matter density, analogous to voids, filaments, and haloes. We model the DM contribution from each substructure and compare it with the simulated DMs to infer the density estimator, the ratio of electron number to total matter density. The resulting overdetermined system is solved in a Bayesian framework with a simulation-physics-informed model. To demonstrate observational applicability, we create a Euclid-like mock galaxy catalogue and build a density estimator based on luminous matter along FRB sightlines. We apply a bias correction for the underlying dark matter distribution and compare the two density estimators to recover the electron number density across the eight bins. Electrons are predominantly localised in low-density regions, while the ensemble mean across all bins aligns with the global theoretical estimate. Combining the FRB and galaxy density estimators, we recover the density of ionised baryons as $Ω_b f_{ion} = 0.0455^{+0.0028}_{-0.0026}$ (simulation: 0.0462), corresponding to $Ω_b = 0.0479^{+0.0029}_{-0.0027}$ for $f_{ion}=0.95$. Our bin-wise electron density estimate reproduces the simulation ground truth to within 10 per cent and gives gas fractions of $0.186 \pm 0.012$, $0.179 \pm 0.015$ and $0.046 \pm 0.014$ in voids, filaments and haloes, against ground truths of 0.167, 0.173 and 0.067.

entries.title: Bar formation and secular evolution in live Milky Way-like galaxies
entries.abstract: Context. Bars and their boxy/peanut (B/P) shapes drive the secular evolution of disc galaxies, redistributing angular momentum and reshaping the radial and vertical structure of stellar discs. Bars occur in bulgeless to bulge-dominated hosts. Bars are known to grow and slow down, but how this relates to host galaxy structure remains poorly understood. Aims. We investigate how the formation and evolution of bars and B/P structures depend on the initial stellar mass and bulge fraction of Milky Way (MW)-like galaxies, and explore the links between disc kinematic settling, bar formation, resonance structure, and vertical thickening. Methods. We analyse fifteen isolated MW-like hydrodynamical simulations run with AREPO for 3 Gyr, spanning three stellar masses and five bulge fractions, with live stellar, bulge, and dark matter components. We measure bar properties via Fourier decomposition, locate resonances from circular and epicyclic frequencies, and quantify B/P evolution from the vertical stellar distribution. Results. Bar formation timing depends strongly on galaxy structure. Low-mass galaxies generally form bars only after global disc kinematics have settled, whereas the most massive systems can form bars while the orbital distribution is still evolving. All bars slow down and grow in strength and size, and remain in the slow-bar regime. B/P structures form shortly after the bar and keep growing, appearing much earlier in more massive and disc-dominated galaxies. Only one model shows a clear buckling event; the rest form B/P bulges through smooth secular evolution. Conclusions. Initial stellar mass and bulge fraction strongly regulate the timing of bar and B/P formation. We find a coherent evolutionary sequence linking bar growth, bar slowdown, and B/P assembly, whose timing is set by the initial disc structure rather than by its global kinematic settling.

entries.title: LEMUR: A Searchable Web Archive of Deep Chandra Images of Galaxies and Galaxy Clusters
entries.abstract: We present LEMUR, a publicly accessible archive of uniformly reduced, deep Chandra images of 2,569 galaxies and galaxy clusters (including groups), comprising 5,505 ACIS observations and 138.8 Ms of exposure. By combining the publicly available imaging observations of each target, we provide background-subtracted, exposure-corrected images in broad, soft, and hard bands at the native ACIS pixel scale of 0.492 arcsec. Our primary goal is to make the wealth of archival Chandra observations accessible to researchers without requiring specialized expertise in X-ray data reduction. Each observation is reprocessed with CIAO, filtered for background flares, and reduced with settings chosen to preserve faint diffuse emission; the merged images are exposure corrected and background subtracted using the ACIS blank-sky backgrounds in a broad (0.5-7.0 keV), a soft (0.5-2.0 keV), and a hard (2.0-7.0 keV) band. For every object, we measure an X-ray center at the peak of its diffuse emission, and we provide a morphological similarity search based on embeddings from the AstroCLIP foundation model, in which nearest neighbors share cool-core status in 73% of matched cluster pairs, compared with 51% by chance. Photometry of 275 point sources agrees with the Chandra Source Catalog to within 3% in the broad band. The images, along with their counts images, background models, exposure maps, and quick-look stamps, are available through a searchable web archive at https://lemur-archive.lemur-xray.workers.dev/. The catalog tables are archived on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24351915), and all code is open source at https://github.com/crhea93/Lemur.

analysis.reason: This paper develops a dimension-free, problem-independent adaptive mesh refinement criterion based on a higher-order ($N=4$) smoothness indicator for Newtonian, SRMHD, and GRMHD simulations. It provides valuable numerical methodology improvements for simulating relativistic blast waves, magnetohydrodynamic instabilities, and black hole accretion flows (SANE/MAD) relevant to high-energy central engines.
analysis.result: The AMR criterion achieves runtime speedups of $1.45\times - 3.66\times$ across Newtonian and SRMHD benchmarks: in the Shu–Osher test, MeshBlock cycles decrease by $4.26\times$ with a $1.72\times$ speedup; in SRMHD magnetic rotor tests, MeshBlock cycles are reduced by $3.4\times$ with a $2.8\times$ speedup at an effective resolution of $1536^2$. In GRMHD Kerr black hole accretion simulations with spin $a/M_{\rm BH}=0.9$, the algorithm tracks turbulent MRI accretion streams and outflows in SANE ($W_{\rm max}=20$, base grid $96^3$) and successfully resolves magnetic flux eruption dynamics in MAD where the horizon dimensionless flux reaches $\phi_{\rm BH} = \Phi_{\rm BH} / \sqrt{\dot{M}} \gtrsim 15$.
analysis.problem: Traditional curvature-based AMR refinement criteria, such as the Löhner-type indicator, rely heavily on empirical threshold tuning and problem-dependent choice of variables, making them difficult to generalize across multi-scale relativistic MHD problems and black hole accretion environments without incurring excessive computational overhead.

analysis.reason: This paper establishes a novel unseen-species statistical framework on CHIME/FRB repeaters, ruling out steady Poisson activity at $p < 10^{-4}$ and demonstrating that repeating FRBs go quiet on a timescale of a few years.
analysis.result: Steady Poisson repeater activity is excluded at $p < 10^{-4}$, with the predicted-to-observed burst ratio dropping from $R(\Delta \le 60\ \mathrm{days}) \approx 1$ to $R(\Delta = 360\ \mathrm{days}) = 0.57 \pm 0.11$, giving an activity ratio $S = 0.530 \pm 0.142$. Fitting cessation models yields an active lifetime $\tau = 2.9^{+1.1}_{-0.9}\ \mathrm{yr}$ for a single-lifetime model, an on/off model with active duration $T_{\rm on} = 800^{+400}_{-400}\ \mathrm{days}$ and duty cycle $d = 0.3^{+0.05}_{-0.2}$, or a mixture model with short lifetime $\tau_s = 500^{+300}_{-200}\ \mathrm{days}$ and long-lived fraction $\eta = 0.3^{+0.2}_{-0.1}$. For an FRB volumetric rate $\mathcal{R}_{\rm FRB} = 7.3 \times 10^4\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the required birth rate satisfies $\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm birth}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm mag}} \sim 0.1\left(\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm FRB}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm CCSN}}\right)\left(\frac{0.1}{f_{\rm b}}\right)\left(\frac{0.4}{f_{\rm mag}}\right)\left(\frac{100\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}}{\bar{r}}\right)$.

analysis.problem: Whether repeating fast radio burst (FRB) sources maintain stationary burst rates indefinitely or cease activity within months to years as predicted by magnetar central engine models.
analysis.method: Formulates an unseen-species estimation framework utilizing Robbins formula $n^{\rm pred}_k = (k+1) N_{k+1} \frac{T_B}{T_A}$ across time windows of length $W = 180\ \mathrm{d}$ separated by gap $\Delta$, evaluating the gap statistic $R(\Delta) = \frac{\sum_s \sum_{k=1}^3 n^{\rm obs}_k(s)}{\sum_s \sum_{k=1}^3 t(s)(k+1)N_{k+1}(s)}$ and decay ratio $S = \frac{R(\Delta \geq 360\ \mathrm{d})}{R(\Delta \leq 90\ \mathrm{d})}$, with exposure calibrated via the Good–Toulmin estimator $N_{\rm new} = \sum_{k \geq 1} (-1)^{k+1} t^k N_k$.
assumptions: Each source is initially assumed to emit bursts following a steady Poisson process with constant mean rate $r$ drawn from rate distribution $f(r)$.
limits: The statistical measurement directly applies only to repeating sources, whereas truly one-off events enter neither observed counts nor predictions.

analysis.reason: SN 2025wiu provides exceptional multi-band photometric and spectroscopic coverage of an extraordinary Type Ib supernova with a post-maximum bump, providing quantitative constraints on shock cooling, central engine activity, and circumstellar medium interaction.
analysis.result: SN 2025wiu displays peak absolute magnitudes of $M_u = -17.5\pm 0.1$, $M_g = -18.11\pm 0.01$, and $M_r = -18.24\pm 0.04\,\mathrm{mag}$, accompanied by early shock cooling from a compact progenitor with $R_\star \approx 4\,R_\odot$, $M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 2\,M_\odot$, and $E \approx 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$. At $\sim 50\,\mathrm{days}$ post-maximum, it develops a secondary bump peaking at $L_{\mathrm{peak}} \sim 2.4\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with total radiated energy $E_{\mathrm{bump}} \sim 10^{49}\,\mathrm{erg}$ and duration $\Delta t \approx 42\,\mathrm{days}$. Synthesized $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ mass estimated from the primary peak via Arnett's rule is $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} \approx 0.47\,M_\odot$, contrasting sharply with late-time radioactive tail deposition ($f_{\mathrm{dep}}(t) = 1 - \exp[-(T_0/t)^2]$ with $T_0 = 173^{+44}_{-41}\,\mathrm{days}$) which yields $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.13^{+0.05}_{-0.02}\,M_\odot$. The bump energy implies an interacting CSM mass of $M_{\mathrm{CSM}} \sim 0.03\,M_\odot$ at radius $R \sim 5\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{cm}$.

analysis.problem: Investigating whether the high peak luminosity and prominent post-maximum bump of the slowly evolving Type Ib supernova SN 2025wiu can be reconciled with standard radioactive decay, or whether delayed circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction, magnetar spin-down, fallback accretion, or a double-$^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ distribution is required.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch optical and NIR photometry combined with optical spectroscopy, analytical $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ radioactive decay modeling via the Arnett rule and deposition function $f_{\mathrm{dep}}(t) = 1 - \exp[-(T_0/t)^2]$, photon diffusion timescale constraints ($t_{\mathrm{d}} = \sqrt{3\kappa M_{\mathrm{ej}} / (4\pi v_{\mathrm{ej}} c)}$), shock cooling emission modeling, and semi-analytical decomposed light-curve fitting involving CSM interaction and magnetar spin-down models.
assumptions: Circumstellar medium interaction converts kinetic energy to radiation with efficiency $\eta = 0.5$ at relative ejecta-CSM velocity $v_{\mathrm{rel}} \approx 8000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$
limits: Persistently weak spectral line features and absence of narrow emission lines up to $\sim 110\,\mathrm{days}$ post-maximum limit direct spectroscopic detection of unshocked circumstellar material

analysis.reason: This paper investigates the dual gamma-ray components of middle-aged SNR IC 443 detected by LHAASO, modeling hadronic emission from SNR-molecular cloud interactions and leptonic emission from the associated PWN, providing direct constraints on Galactic cosmic-ray acceleration and TeV halo formation.
analysis.result: For compact component C0, the SNR-MC hadronic model reproduces the observed SED with a clear $\pi^0$-decay peak, yielding a proton injection spectral index $s = 2.03$, diffusion suppression factor $\chi = 0.08$, and momentum cutoff $p_{\rm cut} = 5.0\times 10^5\text{ GeV}/c$, confirming C0 as a potential Galactic PeVatron candidate. For extended component C1, leptonic inverse Compton scattering from PWN CXOU J061705.3+222127 electrons reproduces the emission with spin-down luminosity $L_{\rm age} = 1.0\times 10^{36}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$, magnetic field $B_{\rm age} = 4.7\ \mu\text{G}$, electron injection index $s = 1.90$, and energy cutoff $E_{\rm cut} = 1.75\times 10^5\text{ GeV}$, requiring strongly suppressed diffusion $D_1 = 1\times 10^{26}\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$ with Bohm scaling $\delta = 1$, identifying C1 as a candidate TeV halo.
analysis.problem: Disentangling the distinct physical origins and radiation mechanisms of the compact component C0 and the extended component C1 (angular scale $\sim 0.67^\circ$) in the middle-aged supernova remnant IC 443.
analysis.method: The authors apply two independent transport and emission models: (1) An SNR-MC hadronic model for C0 accounting for diffusive shock acceleration and energy-dependent proton escape with spectrum $N_{\rm esc}(p) = N_0 p_{\rm br,1}^{-\beta/\alpha} p^{-s}$ ($p \le p_{\rm br,1}$) and $N_0 p^{-(s+\beta/\alpha)} \exp(-p/p_{\rm cut})$ ($p > p_{\rm br,1}$), integrated over a molecular cloud shell $F(p) = \eta \int_{L_1}^{L_2} f(t_{\rm age}, r, p) 4\pi r^2 dr$ with $\beta = 3(3-s)/2$ and $\alpha = 6.5$. (2) A spherically symmetric multi-zone leptonic Fokker-Planck transport model for C1 incorporating spatial diffusion $D(p) = 10^{28}\chi (cp/10\text{ GeV})^\delta\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$, advection, and radiative cooling $\dot{E}_{e,\rm rad} = \frac{4}{3}\sigma_{\rm T} c \left(\frac{E_e}{m_e c^2}\right)^2 [U_B + U_{\rm rad}]$ from the central pulsar wind nebula.

analysis.reason: The paper develops AttNPE, an attention-based neural posterior estimation framework that drastically accelerates cosmological parameter inference from localized FRB dispersion measures while providing redshift-dependent interpretability.
analysis.result: On 120 localized FRBs ($z \le 2.148$), AttNPE reproduces MCMC posteriors with Jensen-Shannon divergence $\mathrm{JSD} < 0.0043$, measuring the IGM dispersion amplitude $\mathcal{A} = 3.221^{+0.224}_{-0.232}\,\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ (MCMC: $3.229^{+0.209}_{-0.224}\,\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$) while generating $5\times 10^4$ posterior samples in $0.03\,\mathrm{s}$ on GPU. Independent simulation validation yields well-calibrated posteriors (KS test $p > 0.05$ for marginal PP and joint TARP metrics), showing that sources at $0.3 \le z < 0.7$ contribute $46.2\%$ of total attention weight and $>40\%$ of shifts in $\Omega_{\rm m}$, $\Omega_{\rm b}$, and $H_0$.

analysis.problem: Traditional Bayesian MCMC inference for FRB cosmology suffers from severe computational bottlenecks due to repeated numerical convolutions over Galactic halo, host galaxy, and IGM dispersion distributions, and standard neural estimators lack physical interpretability regarding how individual bursts at various redshifts constrain cosmological parameters.

analysis.reason: This work presents 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer simulations of the kilonova AT2017gfo, demonstrating that mass scaling and velocity compression of dynamical ejecta self-consistently reproduce the bolometric light curve and early multi-epoch spectra without requiring an ad hoc separate lanthanide-poor component.
analysis.result: By scaling the ejecta mass to $M = 0.04\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ and halving expansion velocities (with half the mass concentrated at radial velocities $v_{r} \lesssim 0.09c$ and peak density at $0.04c$), the 3D model reproduces the bolometric luminosity and optical-to-NIR spectra of AT2017gfo at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$, $2.4\,\mathrm{d}$, and $3.4\,\mathrm{d}$ across $5500\text{--}15\,000\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. The reduced velocity compresses the ejecta density, raising the $\gamma$-ray thermalization efficiency at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$ from $\sim 0.3$ to $\sim 0.55$ and boosting deposited power by $\sim 30\%$ at $1\text{--}4\,\mathrm{d}$. Through the effective temperature scaling $T_{\mathrm{eff}} \propto L^{1/4}(v_{\mathrm{ph}}t)^{-1/2}$, smaller photospheric radii $R_{\mathrm{ph}} = v_{\mathrm{ph}}t$ maintain higher photospheric temperatures and avoid premature reddening. Key spectroscopic identifications include: $\mathrm{Sr\ II}\ \lambda\lambda 10037, 10327, 10915$ generating the $\sim 10\,500\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ NIR peak; $\mathrm{Y\ II}\ \lambda 7882$ contributing to the $\sim 7300\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ peak; $\mathrm{La\ III}\ \lambda\lambda 13894, 14096$ and $\mathrm{Gd\ III}\ \lambda 14333$ forming the $\sim 13\,500\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ shoulder; and $\mathrm{Sr\ II}\ \lambda 4216$ creating the blue flux cutoff at $\lesssim 4500\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. In contrast, 2D azimuthally averaged models are dimmer by a factor of $\sim 3$ at $\sim 1\,\mathrm{d}$ because azimuthal averaging artificially mixes lanthanide-poor channels ($X_{\mathrm{lan}} < 10^{-3}$) with high-opacity lanthanides.
analysis.problem: First-principles numerical relativity simulations yield 3D dynamical ejecta with masses ($M \approx 0.005\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) and expansion velocities ($v_{\mathrm{max}} \approx 0.48c$) that are too low in mass and too high in speed compared to empirical AT2017gfo inferences ($M \approx 0.03\text{--}0.05\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$), causing synthesized light curves to decay prematurely and spectra to peak at overly red or Doppler-shifted wavelengths; furthermore, whether a physically distinct, unmixed lanthanide-poor component is strictly needed to explain the early blue emission remains unresolved.
analysis.method: Multi-dimensional time-dependent Monte Carlo radiative transfer code ARTIS applied to a 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) binary neutron star merger model ($2 \times 1.35\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$, SFHo equation of state) mapped at $t_{\mathrm{snap}} = 0.1\,\mathrm{d}$. Bound-bound transitions ($4.9 \times 10^{7}$ transitions across 83 elements, $Z=57\text{--}70$ in AD3) are computed under local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). Radiative transfer is evaluated across line-by-line (LBL) Sobolev optical depths $\tau_i$, expansion opacities $\kappa_{\mathrm{exp}} = \frac{1}{ct\rho}\sum_i \frac{\lambda_i}{\Delta\lambda}(1 - e^{-\tau_i})$, and capped line-binned opacities with optical depth threshold $\tau_{\mathrm{l,max}}$ where bin optical depth is $\tau_{\mathrm{bin}} = \sum_i \min(\tau_i, \tau_{\mathrm{l,max}})$ and transmission probability $P_0 = e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{bin}}}$.
assumptions: All radiative transfer calculations assume local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) at every timestep to compute level populations and ionization fractions via the Saha and Boltzmann relations.
limits: The uniform velocity compression factor ($v \to v/2$) serves as an empirical proxy for slower post-merger accretion disk wind outflows rather than a dynamically consistent hydrodynamical simulation.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first simultaneous detection and decoupling of relativistic disc reflection and an evolving persistent accretion component during a bright thermonuclear X-ray burst in SAX J1808.4-3658, providing compelling spectroscopic evidence for burst-induced accretion disc puffing.
analysis.result: Using NICER observations of the PRE thermonuclear burst, Model C simultaneously models reflection and persistent emission evolution, finding an enhanced persistent factor $f_{a,1} = 59.6 \pm 0.6$ and reflection fraction $f_{r,1} = 0.82 \pm 0.15$ with a sub-Eddington peak bolometric luminosity of $L_{\mathrm{burst,1}} \approx 0.68\,L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$. The disc ionization parameter drops from $\log \xi = 3.44^{+0.06}_{-0.17}$ at the first peak to $3.09^{+0.19}_{-0.14}$ at the second peak, while the burst blackbody temperature evolves from $kT_{\mathrm{burst}} = 2.25 \pm 0.05\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($R_{\mathrm{burst}} = 8.51 \pm 2.44\,\mathrm{km}$) to $2.15^{+0.07}_{-0.06}\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($R_{\mathrm{burst}} = 7.66 \pm 2.22\,\mathrm{km}$). In the burst tail ($>200\,\mathrm{s}$), column density increases by $\approx 34\%\text{--}46\%$ ($N_{\mathrm{H}} = (2.42^{+0.13}_{-0.10}) \times 10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$) and the disc blackbody temperature increases by $\approx 15\%$, confirming geometric disc puffing that obscures the neutron star surface.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a forward-modeling and Bayesian reconstruction framework to deconstruct FRB dispersion measures into density regimes of the cosmic web, providing quantitative constraints on missing baryons in diffuse IGM/WHIM phases.
analysis.result: The reconstruction recovers the total cosmic electron budget within $1.4\%$ ($\\langle r_{\mathrm{FRB}}\\rangle_M = (0.986 \pm 0.005)\,r_{\mathrm{theo}}$ with theoretical reference $r_{\mathrm{theo}} \approx (7.84 \pm 0.18) \times 10^{22}\,\mathrm{g}^{-1}$) and measures the ionized baryon density $\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}f_{\mathrm{ion}} = 0.0455^{+0.0028}_{-0.0026}$ (matching the simulation ground truth of $0.0462$ within $0.2\sigma$, corresponding to $\Omega_{\mathrm{b}} = 0.0479^{+0.0029}_{-0.0027}$ for $f_{\mathrm{ion}} = 0.95$). Gas mass fractions across large-scale structure environments are determined to be $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{void}} = 0.186 \pm 0.012$, $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{filament}} = 0.179 \pm 0.015$, and $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{halo}} = 0.046 \pm 0.014$, showing that $\sim 75\%$ of free electrons reside in low-density regimes with $\rho_{\mathrm{m}}/\rho_{\mathrm{crit}} \le 2.94$.

analysis.reason: This study models the Galactic population of dormant neutron star binaries and forecasts Gaia DR4/DR5 astrometric yields, providing quantitative constraints on core-collapse supernova engines, natal kicks, and dense matter equations of state.
analysis.result: Under the realistic selection function gaiamock, Gaia is predicted to detect $\sim 100\text{--}110$ and $\sim 300\text{--}380$ dormant neutron star--luminous companion (NS--LC) binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively. In the intrinsic population, $\sim 94\%$ of surviving detached systems survive through common envelope (CE) evolution ($P_{\rm orb} \le 10\,\mathrm{yr}$). The observed NS mass distribution peaks sharply at $1.2\text{--}1.3\,M_\odot$ driven by low-kick ($\sigma = 20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) electron-capture supernovae (ECSN), while delayed core-collapse supernova (CCSN) fallback produces massive NSs exceeding $M_{\rm NS} > 2.5\,M_\odot$ in $\sim 1\%$ of systems. Pulsar spin-down and magnetic field decay follow $\dot{P}_{\rm spin} = K \frac{B^2}{P_{\rm spin}}$ ($K = 9.87 \times 10^{-48}\,\mathrm{yr\,G^{-2}}$), death line $B/P_{\rm spin}^2 = 0.17 \times 10^{12}\,\mathrm{G\,s^{-2}}$, and accretion-induced burial $B = \frac{B_0}{1 + \Delta M / (10^{-6}\,M_\odot)} \exp\left(-\frac{T - t_{\rm acc}}{\tau}\right)$ with $\tau = 3\,\mathrm{Gyr}$.
analysis.problem: Quantifying the Galactic population of dormant neutron stars in detached binaries with luminous companions (NS--LC) detectable via astrometric orbital wobbles in Gaia DR4 and DR5, and testing whether their yields and orbital parameters can break degeneracies between core-collapse supernova explosion models (rapid vs. delayed), natal kicks ($\sigma = 265\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ vs. $20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$), and common envelope evolution.
analysis.method: Binary population synthesis using COSMIC initialized with a Kroupa IMF ($3 < m_{\rm pri}/M_\odot < 60$), flat mass ratios ($q = m_{\rm sec}/m_{\rm pri}$), thermal eccentricities, and log-flat semi-major axes up to $10^5\,R_\odot$. Spatial distribution and star formation histories are drawn from the FIRE-2 m12i Milky Way simulation ($10^{-4} \le Z \le 0.03$). Supernova prescriptions incorporate rapid and delayed core-collapse models (maximum $M_{\rm NS} = 3\,M_\odot$), ECSN ($M_{\rm ZAMS} \sim 8\text{--}10\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm Ch} \approx 1.38\,M_\odot$), and accretion-induced collapse (AIC), followed by synthetic observation through CCB22 and gaiamock astrometric selection functions.
assumptions: The Milky Way binary population follows star formation and metallicity distributions from the FIRE-2 m12i simulation evaluated across 100 Galactic realizations.
limits: The isolated binary evolution models produce no detached millisecond pulsars (MSPs) with main-sequence companions, in contrast to 29 known field radio MSPs in tight orbits from the ATNF pulsar catalog.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first binary population synthesis coupled with time-dependent synchrotron nebular models for hyper-Eddington mass-transfer systems, directly constraining persistent radio source (PRS) counterparts to repeating FRBs, relativistic jet inflation, and radio transient surveys.
analysis.result: The local volumetric birth rate of hyper-Eddington mass-transfer binaries is $\mathcal{R} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ spanning $\dot{m} \sim 10^{2\text{--}7}$ and accretion timescales $t_{\rm acc} \sim 10^{0\text{--}6}\,\mathrm{yr}$. The systems launch mildly relativistic jets ($v_{\rm j} \sim 0.1\text{--}0.3c$) and disk winds ($v_{\rm w} \sim 0.03c$) inflating long-lived synchrotron hypernebulae with peak radio luminosities $L_{\nu,\rm peak} \sim 10^{28}\text{--}10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$ at $\sim 1\text{--}3\,\mathrm{GHz}$, overlapping with FRB-associated PRSs and yielding $\sim 10^{2\text{--}5}$ detectable steady sources in VLASS.
analysis.problem: Distinguishing unresolved synchrotron hypernebulae driven by rare, energetic hyper-Eddington binary mass transfer from other populations of unresolved synchrotron sources (such as AGNs, SNRs, and GRB afterglows) in modern wide-field radio surveys.
analysis.method: Coupled COMPAS binary population synthesis (v02.35.03) with a semi-analytic synchrotron hypernebula model. For stable RLOF, the mass-transfer rate is set by donor envelope thermal timescale $\dot{M} = \dot{M}_{\rm th} = M_{\rm d,env}/\tau_{\rm KH} = R_{\rm d}L_{\rm d}/(G M_{\rm d})$ with duration $t_{\rm acc} = \tau_{\rm KH}$, whereas unstable common-envelope evolution incorporates pre-dynamical accretion $\dot{M} = f_{\rm acc}\Delta M_{\rm CE}/(100 P_{\rm orb})$. Jet kinetic luminosity scales as $L_{\rm j} = \eta L_{\rm w} \simeq \frac{1}{2}\eta \dot{M} v_{\rm w}^2$ with efficiency $\eta \sim 0.1$, injecting relativistic electrons at the termination shock.
assumptions: The donor star transfers its envelope onto a compact object (NS or BH) at hyper-Eddington rates $\dot{M} \gtrsim \dot{M}_{\rm Edd} \equiv L_{\rm Edd}/(0.1c^2)$.
limits: VLBI observations with milliarcsecond-scale resolution are insensitive to diffuse parsec-scale hypernebula structures.

analysis.reason: This paper uses ASKAP POSSUM broadband polarization observations to probe statistical depolarization and Faraday dispersion across the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). It provides valuable empirical constraints on the turbulent magneto-ionic medium and thermal electron density scaling in dwarf irregular galaxies, relevant to intervening sightlines and propagation effects of extragalactic transients.
analysis.result: The fraction of polarized sources is significantly suppressed on-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,on}} = 0.227 \pm 0.021$) compared to off-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,off}} = 0.360 \pm 0.015$), accompanied by an enhanced Faraday depth dispersion $\Sigma_{\phi_{\mathrm{peak}}} = 74 \pm 9\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}}$. Modeling external Faraday dispersion with Burn's law gives $\sigma_\phi = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ with $k = 0.32$, implying a tangled random magnetic field strength $B_r = (1.0 \pm 0.2)\,(l_0/0.5\ \mathrm{pc})^{-1/2}\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ ($B_r \approx 0.3\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ at the beam scale $\sim 6\ \mathrm{pc}$).
analysis.problem: Determining whether depolarization of background radio sources in the SMC is driven by small-scale thermal electron density fluctuations or turbulent random magnetic fields, and assessing whether small-scale Faraday dispersion matches extrapolations of the large-scale RM power spectrum.
analysis.method: Subtracted SMC diffuse emission, performed RM synthesis and Stokes $QU$-fitting on POSSUM Pilot II data ($800-1088\ \mathrm{MHz}$), and modeled external Faraday dispersion $\sigma_\phi = 0.812\,n_e\,B_\parallel\,\sqrt{l_0\,L} = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ combined with $\mathrm{H}\alpha$-derived emission measure $\left(\frac{\mathrm{EM}}{\mathrm{cm^{-6}\ pc}}\right) \approx 2.75 \left(\frac{I_{\mathrm{H}\alpha,\mathrm{corr}}}{\mathrm{R}}\right) \left(\frac{T_e}{10^4\ \mathrm{K}}\right)^{0.942}$.
assumptions: Thermal electron density $n_e$ is assumed to be approximately constant across small scales, attributing Faraday dispersion primarily to random magnetic field fluctuations.
limits: Faraday complexity and multi-component structures are predominantly intrinsic to background sources or foreground Milky Way emission rather than SMC magneto-ionic turbulence.

figures.caption: Figure 9: Peak fractional polarisation against emission measure. The polarised catalogue coloured by their PI SNR (circles), with $1\sigma$ error bars. Sources are binned four per order of magnitude in EM, bin medians (white circles) and means (black triangles) are shown with 68% intervals. Both lines are maximum-likelihood fits to the individual sources in $\ln p_{\mathrm{peak}}$, the blue dashed line is a power law, $p\propto\mathrm{EM}^{\,b}$. The red solid line is the Burn model, $p=p_{0}\,\exp(-2k^{2}\langle\lambda^{4}\rangle\,\mathrm{EM})$, i.e. $\sigma_{\phi}=k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$, with $\langle\lambda^{4}\rangle=0.0110$ m 4 the band average. Shaded regions are the 68% bootstrap ranges of each fit. The black dashed line marks $p_{\mathrm{peak}}=0.01$.
figures.label: Fig. 9
figures.physical_core: Quantifies peak fractional polarisation ($p_{\mathrm{peak}}$) as a function of emission measure (EM), comparing polarimetric observations with maximum-likelihood fits of a power law ($p \propto \mathrm{EM}^b$) and the Burn depolarisation law ($p = p_0 \exp[-2k^2 \langle\lambda^4\rangle \mathrm{EM}]$ with Faraday dispersion $\sigma_\phi = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ and band average $\langle\lambda^4\rangle = 0.0110~\mathrm{m^4}$). This establishes that depolarisation in the SMC systematically increases with EM and is predominantly driven by turbulent magnetic field fluctuations.

must_read.label: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
must_read.text: AT 2025abao is an AGB-star common-envelope merger ($M_1 \approx 7\,M_\odot$, $M_2 \approx 0.7\,M_\odot$, $q \approx 0.10_{-0.05}^{+0.10}$) exhibiting an optical eruption with peak luminosity $L \approx 2.5 \times 10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, an $\approx 80\,\mathrm{d}$ plateau, and ejecta-CSM shock interaction with $v_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}$ decelerating from $\approx 900\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ to $\approx 150\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ matching $\rho(r) \propto r^{-2}$.

must_read.label: The Population of Radio Hypernebulae from Mass-Transferring Massive Binaries
must_read.text: The local volumetric birth rate of hyper-Eddington mass-transfer binaries is $\mathcal{R} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ spanning $\dot{m} \sim 10^{2\text{--}7}$ and accretion timescales $t_{\rm acc} \sim 10^{0\text{--}6}\,\mathrm{yr}$.

must_read.label: A Butterfly Collector's View of Fast Radio Bursts: Repeating Sources Go Quiet within a Few Years
must_read.text: Steady Poisson repeater activity is excluded at $p < 10^{-4}$, with the predicted-to-observed burst ratio dropping from $R(\Delta \le 60\ \mathrm{days}) \approx 1$ to $R(\Delta = 360\ \mathrm{days}) = 0.57 \pm 0.11$, giving an activity ratio $S = 0.530 \pm 0.142$.

must_read.label: SN 2025wiu: A Slowly Evolving Type Ib Supernova with an Extraordinary Post-maximum Bump
must_read.text: SN 2025wiu displays peak absolute magnitudes of $M_u = -17.5\pm 0.1$, $M_g = -18.11\pm 0.01$, and $M_r = -18.24\pm 0.04\,\mathrm{mag}$, accompanied by early shock cooling from a compact progenitor with $R_\star \approx 4\,R_\odot$, $M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 2\,M_\odot$, and $E \approx 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$.

must_read.label: Early spectra of AT2017gfo from scaled 3D merger ejecta: mass--velocity distribution, 3D structure, and treatment of line opacity
must_read.text: By scaling the ejecta mass to $M = 0.04\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ and halving expansion velocities (with half the mass concentrated at radial velocities $v_{r} \lesssim 0.09c$ and peak density at $0.04c$), the 3D model reproduces the bolometric luminosity and optical-to-NIR spectra of AT2017gfo at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$, $2.4\,\mathrm{d}$, and $3.4\,\mathrm{d}$ across $5500\text{--}15\,000\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$.

must_read.label: Investigating the Impact of SAX J1808.4-3658's Very Bright Thermonuclear X-ray Burst on the Accretion Disc with NICER
must_read.text: Using NICER observations of the PRE thermonuclear burst, Model C simultaneously models reflection and persistent emission evolution, finding an enhanced persistent factor $f_{a,1} = 59.6 \pm 0.6$ and reflection fraction $f_{r,1} = 0.82 \pm 0.15$ with a sub-Eddington peak bolometric luminosity of $L_{\mathrm{burst,1}} \approx 0.68\,L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$.

key_highlights.title: Gaia's promise to detect compact-object binaries II: Predictions for dormant neutron star binaries in DR4 and beyond
key_highlights.result: Under the realistic selection function gaiamock, Gaia is predicted to detect $\sim 100\text{--}110$ and $\sim 300\text{--}380$ dormant neutron star--luminous companion (NS--LC) binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively.

key_highlights.title: Fast X-ray Transients as Premature-Dissipated Gamma-Ray Bursts with Magnetic-Dominated Jets
key_highlights.result: When $\sigma_0 \lesssim 45$ satisfies $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R_*) < 1$, premature Type II kink dissipation at $R_* \sim 10^{11}\ \mathrm{cm}$ produces $\Gamma \lesssim 50$ and extreme compactness $\ell' = \frac{L\sigma_{\rm T}}{4\pi R_{\rm dis} m_e c^3 \Gamma^3} \sim 10^3\text{--}10^4$.

key_highlights.title: Isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux limits from Carpet-3 experiment data using neural networks with domain adaptation
key_highlights.result: At 90% CL assuming an $E^{-2}$ spectrum, the integral diffuse gamma-ray flux upper limits span from $\Phi_{\gamma} < 3.2 \times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ down to $< 2.8 \times 10^{-14}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ across threshold energies $14 \le \log_{10}(E/\mathrm{eV}) \le 15.75$, with proton rejection $< 1.3 \times 10^{-5}$ to $< 1 \times 10^{-3}$ and photon efficiency $\varepsilon_{\gamma}$ from $0.004$ to $0.84$.
